gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: After six hours of talks, the two sides finally ___ an agreement.
gaps.explanation: reach an agreement/decision is the collocation; 'arrive' would need 'at', which is not in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: It gets bitterly ___ here in January.
gaps.explanation: bitterly cold is the fixed collocation for extremely cold weather.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.
